hero_title: Syrus turns GitHub issues into reviewed pull requests.
hero_body: Delegate work from GitHub and keep the deterministic parts in your hands: repository setup, credentials, queues, retries, rebases, summaries, and the PR that lands back in review.
live_work_sub: From external signal to pull request.
step_issue_body: A GitHub issue, PR comment, schedule, retry, or rebase enters the queue.
step_job_body: Syrus creates the thread, workspace, branch, prompt, logs, and state machine records.
step_agent_body: Claude or Codex runs in the cloned repository with bounded setup and captured output.
step_pr_body: Syrus commits the result, captures the three-dot diff, and opens or updates the pull request.
feature1_body: Runs from outbound GitHub polling, so private deployments do not need inbound callback plumbing.
feature2_body: Jobs, Workflows, Steps, and Runs keep retries, failures, feedback, summaries, and costs auditable.
feature3_body: Use a GitHub App or PAT fallback while agent provider configuration remains under your instance control.
feature4_body: Review comments, CI failures, retries, and rebases become follow-up attempts on the same Job.
workflow_title: The agent writes code; Syrus owns the run.
workflow_body: Every attempt has a visible state, workspace, logs, prompt, provider, captured diff, and PR summary.
why_title: Keep automation close to the repositories it changes.
why_body: Syrus is built for operators who want agent work to pass through their own queues, credentials, audit logs, and deployment boundaries before a pull request appears.
